findings.instruction: REFERENCE_SCOPE: The reference-guided static sculpt has readable irregular body creases and localized trunk/ankle folds, but fine wrinkle density, facial detail and ear-fold complexity remain simplified versus the supplied image. Describe it as an authored procedural interpretation; do not claim photographic reconstruction or fine-detail parity.

V4_PRESENTATION_LIMIT: Actual native V4 frames are darker/browner than Blender previews and the separate proxy ground shadow is heavier/sharper. Keep this recorded as a static integration/lighting experiment; it is not finished-episode lighting or Blender-look parity acceptance.

V4_SHADOW_PROXY_EDGE: A faint dotted horizontal edge is visible behind the trunk toward the right background and in the ground-shadow difference image. Retain this as a known presentation artifact of the separate shadow proxy; it does not invalidate the static GLB/LTC contribution proof.

review.summary: Independently inspected the exact owner reference and all four actual Windows r6 PNGs; each PNG SHA256 matches the job manifest. Previous EAR_CENTER_GATHER and SURFACE_WRINKLE_HIERARCHY errors are resolved. Continuous torso/head/leg/trunk anatomy, four grounded feet, trunk taper and inward curl, mouth-side tusk roots, thin attached ears, small recessed eyes and low-profile nails are readable across views. Warm matte skin and ivory tusks are distinguishable. Actual native V4 images and controls support scoped static GLB/LTC integration with retained presentation warnings. PASS is limited to the reference-guided static procedural elephant; hidden anatomy and 3m scale are inferred, no rig/animation/physics/human acceptance is claimed.

repeat.scope: Repeated renderStill calls in the same browser instance; not a continuous-playback or same-page seek proof

replay_note: These exact PNGs are the reviewed r6 output on the original Windows PC. They are reference examples, not current-source or cross-machine pixel-parity certification. New builds create new hashes and reviews.
